metadata.title: Robinhood Beats Estimates as Prediction Markets Overtake Crypto

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) rose 0.35% premarket after reporting record second-quarter revenue of $1.31 billion, up 32%, and diluted earnings of $0.62 a share against the $0.43 analysts expected. About $0.14 of that came from gains tied to the deconsolidation of Robinhood Ventures Fund I.
Event contracts revenue reached $156 million, up more than tenfold on 13.6 billion contracts traded. Equities revenue nearly doubled to $129 million and options rose 29% to $342 million. Crypto went the other way, down 38% to $100 million, with notional volume on the Robinhood app falling 35%.
The rest were records. Net deposits reached $21.7 billion, Gold subscribers hit 4.8 million and total platform assets rose 32% to $369 billion. Funded customers grew 7% to 28.4 million and the margin book more than doubled to $21.6 billion. Trump Accounts, which launched on July 4 after the quarter closed, have drawn more than 7 million sign-ups and nearly $1.5 billion in deposits.
Robinhood also lowered its 2026 adjusted operating expense and share-based compensation outlook to $2.675 billion to $2.775 billion from $2.7 billion to $2.825 billion.
